paragraphs: Baker, here is what stands out to me. David was already anointed (1 Samuel 16:13), and he still asked the LORD before he took one step: "Should I go up to one of the towns of Judah?" Then he asked again, "Where should I go?" (2 Samuel 2:1). He didn't pick a spot and hope for the best, and the LORD answered, "To Hebron."

Now look at the two sides. Abner took Saul's son Ish-bosheth, moved him to Mahanaim, and made him king over all Israel (2 Samuel 2:8-9). At Hebron, the men of Judah anointed David king over the house of Judah (2 Samuel 2:4). Then David sent messengers to Jabesh-gilead to bless them for burying Saul (2 Samuel 2:5).

So what do we take home, friend? When you have a big decision, ask God first, even when you think you already know the answer. Be kind to people along the way, because David had a crown coming and still took time to say thank you. And the story isn't over, because Ish-bosheth is on the throne of Israel and David is in Hebron, and I'm not telling you what happens next (2 Samuel 2:10-11).
